**Confirmed [65] numbers**: JACS Au 2021 (PMC8479866) Table 2 gives composition ox/red windows: LPS 1.72–2.30; LGPS 1.63–2.14; LIPON 0.68–2.64; LLZO 0.05–2.68; LLTO 1.71–3.36; LATP 2.17–3.86; LAGP 2.71–3.98. The draft's table note says "LPS 1.72–2.30 V; LGPS 1.63–2.14 V; LLZO 0.05–2.68 V; LiPON 0.68–2.64 V; LLTO 1.71–3.36 V [65]" — **all match**. Good, that's verified.

Note: the draft's stability table 1.5 has "LLZO | ~0 V (kinetic passivation) | ~4.3 V observed (80 °C) | [65,21,26]" — as noted, [65] says LLZO oxidation 2.68 V (thermodynamic) while the table's "~4.3 V observed (80 °C)" comes from [26]. Citing [65] for an observed 4.3 V is a mismatch. The table header says "DFT unless noted" and the LLZO row notes "observed (80 °C)" — but [65] is a DFT source whose number (2.68 V) contradicts "4.3 V observed". The row should cite [26] for the observed value and optionally [65]/[11] for the DFT ceiling. As-is, a reader checking [65] finds 2.68 V — not 4.3 V — and would be confused; also the doc's own note in the draft says kinetic stability is wider (which is the intended meaning: DFT 2.68/2.91 vs observed 4.3). So it's a citation-grouping mismatch — MINOR-to-MAJOR. I'll call it MINOR (the "observed" label and the note below the table partially explain), but recommend splitting citations.

**Electrive 403** — bot-blocked; the research file already rated the NIO story "high" confidence with "CEO William Li: lack of demand" and "few hundred units". The cited draft's exec summary and table restate this. Given the research file records this from the Electrive article, and the research-file table says [88] Electrive "secondary | high", the "few hundred units / lack of demand" claim rests on a single secondary trade source (though quoting the CEO). For a verification pass: single-source critical claim for the exec-summary's "since discontinued" framing — the discontinuation itself is corroborated by [126] headline + industry file timeline ("updated 150 kWh pack reported in 2026"). "Lack of demand" as the reason is single-source (CEO quote via Electrive). Should be attributed ("per NIO CEO via Electrive") — the cited draft says "(lack of demand)" without attribution. MINOR.

Now, remaining checks:
1. The exec summary "no company sells a full-solid-state automotive battery [123]" — citation mismatch (QS B1 press release). Also the internal Blue Solutions/prologium tension. Confirmed as issues to flag.
2. Check ProLogium ">600k cells shipped" — [190] CES 2026. Actually let me not spend too much; the key flag is the Blue Solutions tension.
3. Check QuantumScape table: "QSE-5 B1 samples (>800 Wh/L, 5 Ah)" — quick check of [123] press release. Actually the research file likely verified. Skip; not in task focus.
4. Check the exec summary claim 4 list: "NIO/WeLion 150 kWh pack — since discontinued [126]" — consistent with Electrive.
5. Also verify the LGPS ~1.7–2.1 V window claim [11] — from Han 2016: LGPS window? The Han paper: LGPS oxidation ~2.14 V? Let me grep han2016.txt for LGPS window values to check the draft's "LGPS ~1.7–2.1 V vs Li [3][11]". From the JACS Au: LGPS 1.63–2.14 V. Han 2016: LGPS decomposition at ~1.7 V? Let me check quickly.
6. Check "argyrodites ~2.0–2.5 V vs Li [12]" — TU Delft thesis. Hard to verify; skip (flag as is).
7. Also check the draft's exec summary item 1: "best sulfides and halides now match or exceed liquid-electrolyte conductivity (~10 mS/cm) [66,40,41]" — [66] is the Chem Eng J dry-film paper used for "liquid baseline ~10 mS/cm" — the exec summary cites [66,40,41] for the liquid baseline claim. [66] is a secondary source (dry-film paper) for liquid conductivity — acceptable.

Let me grep Han 2016 for LGPS window values to close that loop, then look at a few more exec-summary citation issues:
- Exec item 3: ">500 Wh/kg claims starting to appear for lithium–sulfur and silicon-based cells [91,92,90]" — [90] = >400 Wh/kg Si. Citation grouping mismatch (MINOR).
- Exec item 5: "analyst projections for 2030 global shipments range from ~509 GWh to 808 GWh [219,220]" — definitional mismatch (CICC includes semi-solid, >650 GWh of the 808 is semi-solid per §4.5). The exec summary doesn't carry that caveat. MINOR/MAJOR? It's a summary of §4.5 which does carry the caveat ("of which semi-solid >650 GWh"). The exec summary's "global shipments" phrasing conflates. MINOR.

Also: I should check the "72 Wh/L" hmm no. Also "Fraunhofer 673 Wh/L / 247 Wh/kg stack with 55 µm membranes [89]" — trust research file.

One more check: the draft's §2.1 says "Liquid baseline: ~1 M LiPF6 in carbonates is ~10 mS/cm class (10⁻² S/cm) [66]" — fine.

Also §1.2 says "A widely cited '2.9 V DFT oxidation limit' for LLZO could not be verified in HTML sources this round and is flagged unverified [materials-gaps]". Given [11] contains 2.91 V, I recommend the draft resolve this. Also worth noting the draft's own [65] gives 2.68 V — the "widely cited 2.9 V" is likely Han 2016's 2.91 V. So this flag is a false negative (overstated uncertainty). This is a MAJOR finding for a verification pass — precisely the kind of "verified/confirmed statements that do not actually show the check" issue... actually reversed: it's an "unverified" statement that is actually verifiable from the draft's own sources.

Also — LGPS ~1.7–2.1 V [3][11]: let me check Han 2016's LGPS window. Also argyrodite 2.0–2.5 V [12]. Let me grep Han for "LGPS" window.

Notably, lower stack pressure suppresses propagation". I recall the Ning 2023 Nature paper indeed found propagation is wedge-driven from the rear (dry crack) and that... lower pressure suppresses propagation? The draft says "Notably, lower stack pressure suppresses propagation — the opposite of the contact-maintenance picture". Hmm — in Ning et al., I believe they found that higher pressures... Let me think. The paper: "Dendrite initiation and propagation in lithium metal solid-state batteries" — they showed initiation via plating into subsurface pores; propagation via wedge opening; and that increased stack pressure actually... I recall the finding that pressure has a non-monotonic effect — moderate pressure helps contact but high pressure exacerbates penetration? Actually I recall their conclusion that "higher stack pressure suppresses void formation but promotes dendrite propagation"? Or the reverse. The draft's claim "lower stack pressure suppresses propagation" — I should verify. Let me quickly check the abstract of Ning 2023.

Actually — [110] Nature Reviews Materials 2024 "External-pressure–electrochemistry coupling" presumably discusses the "stack pressure dilemma". The draft's framing of the dilemma: "lower pressure helps against propagation while higher pressure helps contact". This appears in §3.2 and §5 item 4. Given it's cited to [109,110], let me spot-check Ning's abstract.

Abstract All-solid-state batteries with a Li anode and ceramic electrolyte have the potential to deliver a step change in performance compared with today’s Li-ion batteries1,2. However, Li dendrites (filaments) form on charging at practical rates, penetrate across the ceramic electrolyte leading to short-circuit and cell failure3,4. Previous models of dendrite penetration have generally focused on a single process for dendrite initiation and propagation, with Li driving the crack at its tip5–9. Here we show that initiation and propagation are separate processes. The former arises from filling sub-surface pores with Li via microcracks that connect the pores 1 to the surface. Once filled, further charging builds pressure in the pores due to slow extrusion of Li, (viscoplastic flow) back to the surface, leading to cracking. In contrast, dendrite propagation occurs by wedge-opening, with Li driving the dry crack from the rear not the tip. Whereas initiation is determined by the local (microscopic) fracture strength at the grain boundaries, the pore-size, pore population density and current density, propagation depends on the (macroscopic) fracture toughness of the ceramic, the length of the Li dendrite (filament) that partially occupies the dry crack, current density, stack pressure and the charge capacity accessed during each cycle. Lower stack pressures suppress propagation, markedly extending the number of cycles before short circuit in cells where dendrites have initiated. ## Part 1: Structured Review

## Summary

The artifact is a fully-cited research-round document on solid-state battery electrolytes: four material families, performance benchmarks vs. liquid Li-ion, failure modes, and a mid-2026 commercialization landscape (16-company table, forecasts, cost estimates). Every numbered claim carries an inline citation resolving to a 226-entry Sources list with URL-verification notes; three draft markers (`[materials-gaps]`, `[benchmarks-gaps]`, `[industry-gaps]`) were retained verbatim to flag claims the research files could not verify. The draft's core theses — conductivity is no longer the bottleneck; interfaces/moisture/manufacturing are; every *automotive* product road-tested or mass-produced to date is semi-solid/quasi-solid; full-solid-state launches cluster 2027–2030 — are internally coherent except where noted below.

## Strengths

- **[S1]** **Semi-solid vs. full-solid-state handling is genuinely honest and is the strongest section.** §4.3 separately flags Factorial FEST as quasi-solid (including the correct editorial note that "first solid-state EV" headlines should read "first quasi-solid"), CATL condensed as semi-solid (per its own chief scientist *and* independent HIU classification), NIO/WeLion as semi-solid, and QuantumScape as a "contested middle" with academic liquid-hybrid classification cited. This is exactly the nuance the task asked to check, and it is done well.
- **[S2]** **Four of the five target unverified claims are flagged correctly and consistently** (32 mS/cm sulfide in §1.1, §2.1, §7; 0.15–0.45 S/cm Li3InCl6 in §2.1 and §7; WeLion capacities in [industry-gaps] and §7; Hyundai Uiwang pilot in the table, §7, and [industry-gaps]). The flags are faithful to the research files' own uncertainty records.
- **[S3]** **Spot-checked numbers that I independently verified all match the draft.** [65]'s DFT windows (LLZO 0.05–2.68 V etc.) match the JACS Au table verbatim; the Ning 2023 "lower stack pressure suppresses propagation" claim is verbatim-supported; the [4] review does contain the 32 mS/cm sentence; the LGPS/LLZO figures in [11]'s full text match §1.1's ranges (within the W7 looseness noted below); the 12/25 mS/cm [1][2] values are the well-known literature values.
- **[S4]** **Negative-space claims are mostly handled with appropriate framing** — "not verified in this round," "inferred-from-review," "(self-reported)," "(unconfirmed)," "PDF-level extraction needed" — and §7's "Caveats, confidence, and blocked items" is an unusually candid limitations section.
- **[S5]** **Inference labels are present where the draft's own text derives conclusions** (graphite-based SSB rationale, LLTO Li-metal instability, lab-vs-commercial energy-density assessment, §7 summary).

## Weaknesses

- **[W1] MAJOR — The "2.9 V DFT oxidation limit" flag is resolvable from the draft's own reference list.** §1.2 and [materials-gaps] say the figure "could not be verified in HTML sources this round and is flagged unverified," but the draft's own source [11] (Han et al. 2016, Adv. Energy Mater.) states it in its full text: "The oxidation decomposition of LLZO occurs at as low as 2.91 V…" (verified in OSTI full text). The flag is honest about *method* (HTML-only, no PDF parsing) but its conclusion ("unverified") outruns the evidence already sitting in the draft's Sources. Compounding the issue, the same section's table note reports [65]'s **2.68 V** DFT ceiling for LLZO as verified fact — the same quantity, three numbers in play (2.68 V [65], 2.91 V [11], 4.3 V observed [26]), two of them treated inconsistently. The flag should be resolved (cite [11], reconcile with [65]) rather than left as an open gap.
- **[W2] MAJOR — Internal contradiction: "Every mass-produced … 'solid-state' product … is semi-solid/quasi-solid" vs. the draft's own Blue Solutions row.** Exec Summary item 4 claims no company sells a full-solid-state automotive battery and that every mass-produced/road-tested "solid-state" product is semi-solid/quasi-solid. But §4.2's own table says Blue Solutions has been "In production for buses since 2011" with polymer-LMP cells that the manufacturer markets as all-solid-state (verified on [194]), and §4.3 simultaneously lists "Blue Solutions polymer" among "Full-solid-state programs … target 2027–2030." A company can't be both "in production since 2011" and a "program targeting 2027–2030." The claim needs an explicit definition of "automotive" (passenger-car scope), and the Blue Solutions case needs to be reconciled explicitly — either LMP is full-solid-state (then the exec-summary claim needs a passenger-car qualifier) or it isn't (then it should not be listed under full-solid-state programs). The ProLogium ">600k cells shipped" row creates the same unresolved tension.
- **[W3] MAJOR — Negative claims are cited to sources that cannot support them.** "As of mid-2026, no company sells a full-solid-state automotive battery **[123]**" — [123] is a QuantumScape B1-sample press release; a single company's press release cannot establish an industry-wide absence. Same pattern in the GM row: "No own solid-state program found **[203,202]**" — [203] (GM Authority stake sale) and [202] (Korea Times SES interview) do not document the absence of a GM solid-state program. These should be reframed as "none found in this research round" (a survey inference, not a citable fact) or backed by an actual market survey.
- **[W4] MAJOR — Confirmed bibliographic error: two different papers assigned identical journal/volume/pages.** Sources [75] (Krauskopf, "The natural critical current density limit for Li7La3Zr2O12 garnets") and [223] (Doux, "Pressure effects on sulfide electrolytes…") both read "J. Mater. Chem. A 8, 5049–5055 (2020)." Crossref: Doux = 8, 5049–5055 (correct); Krauskopf = 8, **15782–15788**. Two distinct papers cannot share coordinates. This is precisely the class of error the Sources verification note ("Spot-checks of load-bearing claims … all matched") claims to have prevented; the spot-check evidently did not cover bibliographic coordinates.

[119] is intelligentliving.co, which the research file rates "secondary | low-medium" — but the cited draft carries no confidence label on [119], while it does carry "(low-medium confidence)" on [215] WardsAuto. - **[W9] MINOR — The 0.15–0.45 S/cm flag is directionally right but understated and mis-worded.** Verified: the claim exists verbatim in [71]'s abstract (Discover Chemical Engineering, 2024: "superionic conductivity (0.15–0.45 S cm⁻¹)… two magnitudes increase compared to the published data"). ## Questions for Authors

- [Q1] **For the [materials-gaps] flag on "2.9 V":** Han et al. 2016 (your source [11]) states the LLZO oxidation limit as 2.91 V in its full text (OSTI copy). Why was this not resolved against the sources already in your list? Can the flag be replaced with a citation to [11] plus a reconciliation note for [65]'s 2.68 V?
- [Q2] **For the "no company sells" claim:** how is "automotive" defined, and how do Blue Solutions (LMP in production since 2011) and ProLogium (">600k cells shipped") fit that definition? Should the exec summary carry an explicit scope qualifier?
- [Q3] **For [119] (BYD $70/kWh):** the research file rates intelligentliving.co low-medium confidence, but the draft carries no flag. Was there a corroborating source for the $70/kWh figure, and if not, should it be flagged like [215]?

## Verdict

This is a well-constructed research-round document whose epistemic posture is mostly exemplary: it flags what it could not verify, labels inferences, and handles the semi-solid/full-solid-state distinction more honestly than most trade coverage. None of the findings are FATAL — the document's purpose (a cited research round) is served. But the five MAJOR items are revision-required before this can be treated as a trustworthy citation baseline: (1) resolve the 2.9 V flag against the draft's own [11]; (2) reconcile the Blue Solutions/exec-summary contradiction with an explicit "automotive = passenger car" scope; (3) reframe negative claims ("no company sells," GM "no program") as survey inferences rather than citable facts; (4) fix the Krauskopf page range and extend the verification note to cover bibliographic coordinates; (5) add the missing confidence flag to [119]. **Confidence in findings: high** — every MAJOR finding was verified against primary text (Crossref, OSTI, PMC, publisher pages) or traced to the research files' own records. Residual risk is concentrated in the items I could not fetch (Electrive [126], S&P [213], McKinsey [116]) due to bot-blocking; those were assessed via research-file records and cross-references.

## Part 1: Structured Review

## Summary

The artifact is a fully-cited research-round document on solid-state battery electrolytes: four material families, performance benchmarks vs. liquid Li-ion, failure modes, and a mid-2026 commercialization landscape (16-company table, forecasts, cost estimates). Every numbered claim carries an inline citation resolving to a 226-entry Sources list with URL-verification notes; three draft markers (`[materials-gaps]`, `[benchmarks-gaps]`, `[industry-gaps]`) were retained verbatim to flag claims the research files could not verify. The draft's core theses — conductivity is no longer the bottleneck; interfaces/moisture/manufacturing are; every *automotive* product road-tested or mass-produced to date is semi-solid/quasi-solid; full-solid-state launches cluster 2027–2030 — are internally coherent except where noted below.

## Strengths

- **[S1]** **Semi-solid vs. full-solid-state handling is genuinely honest and is the strongest section.** §4.3 separately flags Factorial FEST as quasi-solid (including the correct editorial note that "first solid-state EV" headlines should read "first quasi-solid"), CATL condensed as semi-solid (per its own chief scientist *and* independent HIU classification), NIO/WeLion as semi-solid, and QuantumScape as a "contested middle" with academic liquid-hybrid classification cited. This is exactly the nuance the task asked to check, and it is done well.
- **[S2]** **Four of the five target unverified claims are flagged correctly and consistently** (32 mS/cm sulfide in §1.1, §2.1, §7; 0.15–0.45 S/cm Li3InCl6 in §2.1 and §7; WeLion capacities in [industry-gaps] and §7; Hyundai Uiwang pilot in the table, §7, and [industry-gaps]). The flags are faithful to the research files' own uncertainty records.
- **[S3]** **Spot-checked numbers that I independently verified all match the draft.** [65]'s DFT windows (LLZO 0.05–2.68 V etc.) match the JACS Au table verbatim; the Ning 2023 "lower stack pressure suppresses propagation" claim is verbatim-supported; the [4] review does contain the 32 mS/cm sentence; the LGPS/LLZO figures in [11]'s full text match §1.1's ranges (within the W7 looseness noted below); the 12/25 mS/cm [1][2] values are the well-known literature values.
- **[S4]** **Negative-space claims are mostly handled with appropriate framing** — "not verified in this round," "inferred-from-review," "(self-reported)," "(unconfirmed)," "PDF-level extraction needed" — and §7's "Caveats, confidence, and blocked items" is an unusually candid limitations section.
- **[S5]** **Inference labels are present where the draft's own text derives conclusions** (graphite-based SSB rationale, LLTO Li-metal instability, lab-vs-commercial energy-density assessment, §7 summary).

- **[W1] MAJOR — The "2.9 V DFT oxidation limit" flag is resolvable from the draft's own reference list.** §1.2 and [materials-gaps] say the figure "could not be verified in HTML sources this round and is flagged unverified," but the draft's own source [11] (Han et al. 2016, Adv. Compounding the issue, the same section's table note reports [65]'s **2.68 V** DFT ceiling for LLZO as verified fact — the same quantity, three numbers in play (2.68 V [65], 2.91 V [11], 4.3 V observed [26]), two of them treated inconsistently.
